title: A Hollow for the Crown
premise: Orsen Ashgrove was raised in the Ashen Valley, a place where magic cannot follow, and serves the usurper King Veylan as a food-taster, dosing himself with poisons until his body becomes a ledger of survival. When prayers to the old gods begin to be answered across the realm, Orsen learns he is the last vessel of the Hollow Crown's memory—the living archive of the deposed royal line—and that the gods are answering through him whether he wills it or not. Hunted by Veylan's inquisitors and sheltered by a ragtag found family of deserters, smugglers, and one very stubborn priestess, he must carry the crown's memories to the free cities before Veylan's armies arrive. In the end, Orsen chooses not to restore the old dynasty but to release its memory into the world entirely, dissolving the crown's power and ending the ancient war before it can reignite—at the cost of forgetting the family that made him who he is.
about_author: Theo Hartwell is the pen name of a former line cook turned fantasy writer who swears the best worldbuilding happens over a simmering stockpot. They live somewhere rainy with two cats and an unreasonable collection of antique recipe books.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A routine morning tasting for King Veylan goes wrong when a dish laced with something unfamiliar doesn't kill him—it whispers. Establishes his immunity training, his numbness toward court life, and the first crack in his invisibility. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: What the Valley Forgot
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, flashback-woven. He returns home to the Ashen Valley for his mother's remembrance day, where magic cannot follow him, and realizes the whispering stopped at the valley border. His aunt lets slip that his lineage was never accidental. Emotional beat: grief entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered in the Dark
chapters.summary: Sera's POV—a young priestess of the old gods whose candle-prayers have suddenly begun burning blue. She traces the answered prayers across the city and finds they all point toward the palace kitchens. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear as she realizes someone is being used as a conduit.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Invitation
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Inquisitor Dain Corveth summons him—not about poison, but about dreams. Orsen lies badly and leaves knowing he's marked. That night the crown's first full memory seizes him: a coronation three hundred years dead. Emotional beat: terror of becoming visible.

chapters.title: A Thief in the Pantry
chapters.summary: Wick's POV—a palace smuggler caught stealing saffron by Orsen, who covers for him on instinct. Wick owes him, and more importantly knows the tunnels out of the city. Their wary alliance begins. Emotional beat: unexpected warmth between two people trained to trust no one.

chapters.title: Blood in the Soup Course
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A fellow taster dies from a poison Orsen's body shrugged off—proof someone is targeting him specifically. Sera confronts him in the kitchens; her god speaks through her mouth and calls him 'vessel.' Emotional beat: loneliness shattering as his secret finds witnesses.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Veylan's Shadow
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. Orsen flees the capital through Wick's tunnels with Sera and a deserter named Bram. The crown's memories begin arriving unbidden—battlefields, betrayals, a queen's last words. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure, fragile and improvised.

chapters.title: Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The group shelters in the Ashen Valley, where Orsen goes silent inside—no memories, no whispers—and must decide whether safety means surrendering the mission. Sera argues the gods chose him for a reason. Emotional beat: the seduction of hiding versus the pull of purpose.

chapters.title: The Queen's Last Recipe
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Among his mother's things he finds a recipe book annotated in royal cipher—the crown's memories hide inside recipes, and his family were keepers, generation after generation. He deciphers the first true secret: the location of the free cities' council. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as burden and gift at once.

chapters.title: Corveth Closes In
chapters.summary: Dain Corveth's POV. The inquisitor interrogates Orsen's aunt and pieces together the keeper bloodline, revealing Veylan wants Orsen alive because a vessel's death would scatter the crown's memory forever—or ignite it. Emotional beat: chilling competence; the hunter understands the prize better than the hunted.

chapters.title: Bram's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The deserter secretly offers to sell Orsen's location in exchange for amnesty for his stranded company, then wavers when Orsen shares a memory with him—one of Bram's own dead comrades, preserved in the crown. Emotional beat: betrayal contemplated and refused; loyalty chosen over survival.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Gate
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The group reaches Meridian, first of the free cities, but the council refuses to believe a kitchen servant carries the old dynasty. Sera performs a rite that forces the crown's memory public—and half the council recoils in fear of the war it promises. Emotional beat: hope meeting institutional cowardice.

chapters.title: Poison Politics
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A council faction tries to use Orsen as a figurehead puppet; another tries to poison him, assuming his immunity is legend. It isn't. He survives publicly, and the crowd begins calling him the Hollow Prince. Emotional beat: horror at becoming a symbol he never asked to be.

chapters.title: What Wick Carries
chapters.summary: Wick's POV. Wick confesses he originally scouted Orsen for Corveth to buy his brother's freedom, and has been feeding false reports since. Trust fractures and mends. Emotional beat: confession as the true price of found family.

chapters.title: Veylan's Army Marches
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. News arrives: Veylan's legions are weeks from Meridian, with Corveth riding ahead. The council dithers; Sera's order splits between those who want Orsen enthroned and those who want him silenced. Emotional beat: the walls closing in from every direction at once.

chapters.title: The Hollow Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Under siege of doubt, Orsen opens himself fully to the crown's memory and finally sees the whole truth: the original war began because the crown hoarded memory itself, and the gods went silent rather than serve it. Emotional beat: revelation that the inheritance is the disease, not the cure.

chapters.title: Corveth at the Gate
chapters.summary: Dain Corveth's POV, then Orsen's. Corveth breaches Meridian's lower city and offers Orsen a deal: come quietly, live comfortably, be a vessel in a gilded cage. Orsen refuses—and Corveth, unexpectedly, hesitates, revealing even he fears what the crown could become. Emotional beat: the enemy humanized at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Choice of Vessels
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With Veylan's army days away, the council demands Orsen take up the Hollow Crown physically and lead them to victory. Sera begs him to refuse; Wick tells him whatever he chooses, they'll stand with him. Emotional beat: the loneliest decision, surrounded by people who love him.

chapters.title: Climax: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On the battlefield plain before Meridian, instead of crowning himself, Orsen releases the crown's entire memory into every mind present—king, soldier, councilor alike—so no single vessel, no single throne, can ever hold it again. Veylan's claim collapses; Corveth lowers his blade. Emotional beat: transcendence through relinquishment.

chapters.title: The Cost of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The release takes its price: Orsen's own stored memories bleed out with the crown's. He wakes knowing what he did but not the faces of the people weeping over him. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness—found family grieving a man still breathing beside them.

chapters.title: Recipes Without a Keeper
chapters.summary: Rotating POVs of Sera, Wick, and Bram. They rebuild around Orsen, retelling him their shared history daily like a liturgy, writing it into a new book of recipes so no memory ever depends on one person again. Emotional beat: love as deliberate, repeated labor.

chapters.title: A Table Set for Strangers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue. Months later, Orsen runs a small kitchen in Meridian, immune to poison but not to belonging. Fragments of feeling surface without context—warmth at Wick's laugh, grief at Sera's hymns—and he chooses to let them mean what they mean now. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; inheritance transformed into choice.
